'''Thomas F. Coleman''' (1950–2021)<ref name=inmem>{{cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/combinatorics-and-optimization/contacts/thomas-f-coleman|title=Thomas F. Coleman|work=In memorial|publisher=University of Waterloo Combinatorics & Optimization|access-date=2025-03-12}}</ref> was a Canadian mathematician and computer scientist who is a Professor in the Department of Combinatorics and Optimization at the [[University of Waterloo]],<ref>{{cite web | title=Thomas F. Coleman | website=University of Waterloo | url=https://uwaterloo.ca/scholar/tfcolema/home | access-date=2021-03-23}}</ref> where he held the Ophelia Lazaridis University Research Chair. In addition, Coleman was the director of WatRISQ,<ref>{{cite web | title = About Waterloo Research Institute in Insurance, Securities and Quantitative Finance (WatRISQ)| date = 23 April 2014| url = https://uwaterloo.ca/waterloo-research-institute-in-insurance-securities-and-quantitative-finance/about}}</ref> an institute composed of quantitative and computational finance researchers spanning several Faculties at the University of Waterloo. His research focused on [[mathematical optimization]].

== Education ==
Coleman earned his PhD from [[University of Waterloo]] in 1979 with the dissertation ''A Superlinear Penalty Function Method to Solve the Nonlinear Programming Problem'' supervised by Andrew Conn.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=30199}}</ref> He followed that up with a two-year postdoctoral appointment in the Applied Mathematics Division at [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name=inmem/>

==Career==
From 1981 to 2005, Coleman was a professor of computer science at [[Cornell University]]. From 1998 to 2005 he served as the director of Cornell Theory Center, now [[Cornell University Center for Advanced Computing]]<ref>{{cite web | title=Cornell University Center for Advanced Computing | website=Cornell University Center for Advanced Computing | date=2011-01-25 | url=https://www.cac.cornell.edu/ | access-date=2021-03-23}}</ref>

From 2005 to 2010, Coleman served as the dean of the Faculty of Mathematics at the University of Waterloo. During his tenure as Cornell Theory Center director, Coleman founded and directed a computational finance academic-industry-government venture located at 55 Broad Street in
New York, which shaped into Cornell Financial Engineering Manhattan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.orie.cornell.edu/orie/cfem|title=Financial Engineering Concentration and Cornell Financial Engineering Manhattan (CFEM) &#124; Operations Research and Information Engineering|website=www.orie.cornell.edu}}</ref>

He died of cancer on April 20, 2021.<ref name=inmem/>

== Awards and honors ==
Coleman was selected a [[SIAM Fellow]] in 2016 "for his contributions to financial optimization, sparse numerical optimization and leadership in mathematical education and industry engagement".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/waterloo-research-institute-in-insurance-securities-and-quantitative-finance/news/tom-coleman-selected-siam-fellow|title=Tom Coleman Selected SIAM Fellow|date=April 22, 2016|website=Waterloo Research Institute in Insurance, Securities and Quantitative Finance}}</ref>
